result.rationale: The diff shows `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` after mapping blacklist entries to lowercase, but `guest` is not lowercased, so BLOCKED@x.com bypasses the blacklist. Similarly `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, allowing case-variant duplicates. Both mechanisms are verifiable in addGuests.handler.ts.

judged_text: In addGuests.handler.ts:67-74, email comparisons are case-sensitive: the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is compared as-submitted, so BLOCKED@x.com bypasses blocked@x.com. The same defect exists in the dedup (guest === attendee.email), allowing John@X.com to be added when john@x.com is already an attendee, creating a duplicate person. The abuse-control env var is bypassed by changing one letter's case.
